gap: No result ChatGPT got states that both new-production picks, the TEAC W-1200 and the Tascam 202MKVII, cannot record Type IV metal tape and cannot record with Dolby-style noise reduction. Their noise-reduction switch only cuts hiss on playback. So a shopper who wants to make Dolby-encoded or metal-tape recordings needs a vintage deck.
standout_why: I compared against StereoNET (cited in all 3 chats) and Tape Lab (tapelab.live, cited). Portcycling (cited once) returned HTTP 403, so I could not read it. StereoNET says the W-1200 has noise reduction but does not give the Dolby type. It says nothing about which tape types the W-1200 records, and it never mentions the Tascam 202MKVII. It does say Nakamichi and Revox decks have Dolby B/C, and that metal tape 'demands … a deck that supports it'. Tape Lab mentions neither tape types nor Dolby. Neither page says the new decks' noise reduction works on playback only or that they cannot record metal tape. Neither gives USB operating-system support or says what comes in the box. Our own current page also gets one detail wrong: it lists the 202MKVII with 'no remote', but Tascam's spec page lists a Remote control (RC-1331) × 1 in the box.
decides: This backs up ChatGPT's split, with a reason the rival pages don't give. The W-1200 and 202MKVII are the right picks for playing old tapes and digitizing them over USB. They record only Type I and II tape, and their noise reduction can't be applied while recording. Shoppers who want to record at full quality, using metal tape or Dolby noise reduction, need a serviced vintage 3-head deck. A wiki lists the Sony TC-KA7ES with Dolby B, C and S and Type I/II/IV tape, but I did not get a maker document for it. Between the two new decks, the 202MKVII's maker page lists current Windows 11 and macOS releases. The W-1200's manual lists systems only up to Windows 10 and macOS 10.13, as of November 2017.

findings.label: Tape types: recording vs playback
findings.value: Plays Normal (Type I), Chrome (Type II) and Metal (Type IV). Records Type I and Type II only. The manual says: 'This unit does not support recording to metal (type IV) tapes.'
findings.note: Taken from section 3.1 and the 'Recording to cassette tapes' section of TEAC's owner's manual. I could not load TEAC's own spec page (teac.jp/int/product/w-1200/spec) in text form, and teacusa.com failed with an SSL error.

findings.label: Noise reduction scope
findings.value: Playback only. The manual says: 'This cannot be used when recording to achieve a noise reduction effect like Dolby B.'
findings.note: Per the manual, the NOISE REDUCTION switch 'reduces hiss during tape playback' of tapes recorded with Dolby B. It is a hiss filter, not a Dolby encoder or decoder. The manual mentions no Dolby C or S.

findings.label: USB audio and supported operating systems
findings.value: USB audio up to 48 kHz at 8 or 16 bit. The manual lists Windows 7, 8, 8.1 and 10 (32/64-bit) and Mac OS X 10.7 Lion to macOS 10.13 High Sierra, saying use with other systems 'is not guaranteed (as of November 2017)'. It runs on the standard OS driver, so no driver install is needed.
findings.note: The full sample-rate list is 8, 11.025, 16, 22.05, 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz. The OS list is the 2017 manual's, so newer systems are simply not listed.

findings.label: In the box and pitch control limit
findings.value: Remote control (RC-1331) with 2 AA batteries and 2 RCA audio cables. Pitch control works only during TAPE 1 playback.
findings.note: Contents from section 2.1, pitch control from section 9.5.

findings.label: Tape types: recording vs playback
findings.value: Records and plays Type I (normal) and Type II (chrome). For Type IV (metal), only playback is supported.

findings.label: Noise reduction scope
findings.value: Noise reduction function to reduce hiss during playback (equivalent to Dolby B NR).
findings.note: The maker describes it as playback-only. No recording-side noise reduction is listed.

findings.label: USB audio and supported operating systems
findings.value: USB-B, USB 2.0 Full Speed, 8 to 48 kHz at 8 or 16 bit. Windows: Windows 10 May 2020 Update through 22H2, and Windows 11 21H2 through 25H2. Mac: macOS Big Sur (11) through macOS Tahoe and 'macOS Golden Gate'.
findings.note: From the page's 'Compatible OS' section. The page does not say whether a driver is needed.

findings.label: In the box, rack size, power, function exclusions
findings.value: Box contents: Remote control (RC-1331) with 2 AA batteries, rackmount screw kit and owner's manual. 3U rack mount. AC 120 V 60 Hz for US/Canada (240 V 50 Hz for UK/Europe), 14 W. Pitch control is ±12% on TAPE 1 only. Compared with the 202MKVI it has no auto reverse, no continuous Deck 1/2 recording or playback, and no high-speed dubbing.
findings.note: This contradicts our current page, which says 'no remote'. That cell needs correcting.

findings.label: Noise reduction and tape types (vintage counterpoint)
findings.value: Dolby B, C and S. Tape types I, II and IV. 3 heads. Made 1994 to 1997.
findings.note: Wiki data with no cited spec source, so it is weaker than a maker document. I could not find Sony's manual for the KA7ES.
